purpose: Benzonatate is used to help relieve a dry, non-productive cough. It works to reduce the urge to cough so you can feel more comfortable. It does not treat the underlying cause of your cough, such as an infection, but it helps manage the symptom.
how_it_works: Benzonatate works by numbing or desensitizing the stretch receptors in your lungs and airways that trigger the cough reflex. Think of it like a local anesthetic for the inside of your chest. When those receptors are less sensitive, your brain gets fewer signals telling it to cough.
common_side_effects: You may notice drowsiness, dizziness, or headache. Some people experience mild stomach upset, constipation, or a feeling of numbness in the chest. You might also feel a bit lightheaded or have stuffy nose.
warnings: Never chew, crush, or suck on the capsules — swallow them whole. If the capsule is broken in your mouth, the medicine can numb your mouth and throat and may cause serious problems like choking or a dangerous drop in blood pressure. Keep this medicine away from children, as accidental swallowing of even one capsule can be life-threatening to a small child. Call your doctor right away if you have confusion, hallucinations, or difficulty breathing.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 100 mg to 200 mg taken by mouth three times a day, as needed. Do not take more than 600 mg in one day. Always follow your doctor or pharmacist's specific instructions for your situation.
